docs.title: PHP Source Code Review
docs.text:
PHP applications are particularly useful candidates for source code review because input sources, application logic, database operations, file-system operations, template rendering and dangerous execution functions are often visible directly in application code.

This note focuses on reviewing:

PHP 8.x
Plain / Native PHP
Composer Applications
Laravel
Symfony
CodeIgniter
Slim
WordPress-style PHP applications
Custom PHP frameworks
Legacy PHP applications

The primary objective is to identify attacker-controlled input and determine whether it reaches a security-sensitive operation without an effective security control.

HTTP Request
     |
     v
PHP Input Source
     |
     v
Routing / Controller
     |
     v
Validation
     |
     v
Authentication
     |
     v
Authorisation
     |
     v
Business Logic
     |
     v
SECURITY-SENSITIVE SINK

The basic review model is:

SOURCE
   |
   v
USER-CONTROLLED DATA
   |
   v
TRANSFORMATIONS
   |
   +-- decoding
   +-- parsing
   +-- validation
   +-- normalisation
   +-- sanitisation
   +-- business logic
   |
   v
SECURITY CONTROL
   |
   v
SINK
   |
   v
EXPLOITABILITY

A source-code match is not automatically a vulnerability.

grep match
    !=
vulnerability

Instead:

Candidate Code
      |
      v
Data-Flow Analysis
      |
      v
Reachability
      |
      v
Security Controls
      |
      v
Exploitability
      |
      v
Impact

Authorised Security Testing

Perform source code review and dynamic validation only against applications and repositories for which you have explicit authorisation. Source repositories may contain credentials, API keys, cryptographic material, personal information and internal infrastructure details.

docs.title: Review Strategy
docs.text:
A practical PHP source review can be performed in the following order:

1. Identify the PHP version

2. Identify the framework

3. Inspect Composer dependencies

4. Identify application entry points

5. Enumerate routes

6. Identify authentication

7. Identify authorisation

8. Identify attacker-controlled sources

9. Identify validation

10. Identify dangerous sinks

11. Trace source-to-sink paths

12. Review business logic

13. Review configuration

14. Search for secrets

15. Review dependencies

16. Review templates

17. Run static analysis

18. Perform variant analysis

19. Validate findings dynamically where authorised

docs.title: Identify the Application
docs.text:
Start by understanding the repository.

find . -maxdepth 3 -type f \( \
-name 'composer.json' \
-o -name 'composer.lock' \
-o -name 'artisan' \
-o -name 'symfony.lock' \
-o -name 'wp-config.php' \
-o -name 'index.php' \
-o -name '.env' \
-o -name '.env.example' \
\) -print

Common indicators:

File Possible Technology composer.json Composer-managed PHP artisan Laravel symfony.lock Symfony wp-config.php WordPress application/config/ Older CodeIgniter app/Config/ CodeIgniter 4 vendor/ Composer dependencies .env Environment configuration

docs.title: Identify PHP Version
docs.text:
Check Composer requirements:

rg -n \
'"php"\s*:' \
--glob 'composer.json' \
.

Example:

"require": {
    "php": "^8.3"
}

Also inspect:

Dockerfile
docker-compose.yml
.github/workflows/
.gitlab-ci.yml
composer.json
composer.lock

Search:

rg -n -i \
'php:[0-9]|php-version|FROM php|platform.*php' \
.

Knowing the PHP version matters when reviewing:

Deprecated APIs
Removed APIs
Framework compatibility
Dependency vulnerabilities
Language behaviour
Security defaults

docs.title: Composer
docs.text:
Composer is the primary PHP dependency manager.

Important files:

composer.json
composer.lock

Inspect:

cat composer.json

Search dependencies:

rg -n \
'"require"|"require-dev"|"repositories"|"autoload"|"scripts"' \
composer.json

docs.title: Identify Frameworks
docs.text:
Quick search:

rg -n -i \
'laravel|symfony|codeigniter|slim|cakephp|yii|wordpress|woocommerce' \
composer.json composer.lock 2>/dev/null

docs.title: Laravel
docs.text:
Indicators include:

artisan
app/
bootstrap/
config/
database/
public/
resources/
routes/
storage/

Routes commonly exist in:

routes/web.php
routes/api.php
routes/console.php

docs.title: Symfony
docs.text:
Common structure:

bin/
config/
public/
src/
templates/
var/
vendor/

Routes may exist in:

config/routes.yaml
config/routes/
Controller annotations / attributes

docs.title: Native PHP
docs.text:
Older or custom applications may use:

index.php
login.php
admin.php
api.php
includes/
inc/
lib/
config/

Each PHP file may effectively represent an endpoint.

docs.title: Application Entry Points
docs.text:
Find PHP files:

find . -type f -name '*.php' \
-not -path './vendor/*' \
-not -path './node_modules/*'

Prioritise:

public/index.php
index.php
api.php
login.php
admin.php
upload.php
download.php
callback.php
webhook.php

docs.title: Route Discovery
docs.text: Route discovery depends heavily on the framework.

docs.title: Laravel Routes
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'Route::(get|post|put|patch|delete|options|any|match|resource|apiResource)' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

Route::get(
    '/users/{id}',
    [UserController::class, 'show']
);

Route:

GET /users/{id}

docs.title: Laravel Route Groups
docs.text:
Review:

Route::middleware(['auth'])->group(function () {
    ...
});

Search:

rg -n \
'Route::middleware|Route::prefix|Route::group|middleware\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Route security may be inherited from groups.

Do not review individual routes in isolation.

docs.title: Symfony Routes
docs.text:
Modern Symfony commonly uses attributes:

#[Route('/users/{id}', methods: ['GET'])]
public function show(int $id)
{
    ...
}

Search:

rg -n \
'#\[Route|@Route' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Also inspect:

config/routes.yaml
config/routes/

docs.title: Generic Route Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Route::|#\[Route|@Route|->get\(|->post\(|->put\(|->patch\(|->delete\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Expect false positives.

docs.title: Build a Route Inventory
docs.text:
Create a table:

Method Route Handler Authentication Authorisation GET /users/{id} UserController::show Required Ownership POST /users UserController::store Required Admin POST /login AuthController::login Public N/A POST /upload FileController::upload Required User GET /admin AdminController Required Admin

This route map becomes the basis for the rest of the review.

docs.title: PHP Input Sources
docs.text:
PHP provides several superglobal arrays containing attacker-controlled request data.

The most important are:

$_GET
$_POST
$_REQUEST
$_COOKIE
$_FILES
$_SERVER

Other sources may include:

php://input
HTTP headers
JSON bodies
Route parameters
Session values influenced by previous requests
Database values containing stored user input
Message queues
Uploaded files

docs.title: Search PHP Superglobals
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\$_GET|\$_POST|\$_REQUEST|\$_COOKIE|\$_FILES|\$_SERVER' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

This is one of the highest-value first searches in a PHP application.

docs.title: $_GET
docs.text:
Example:

$id = $_GET['id'];

Source:

GET parameter id

Trace:

$_GET['id']
     |
     v
$id
     |
     v
Application Logic
     |
     v
Sink

docs.title: $_POST
docs.text:
Example:

$username = $_POST['username'];

Trace where the value is used.

docs.title: $_REQUEST
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\$_REQUEST' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

$_REQUEST deserves additional attention because the exact sources included depend on PHP configuration.

Avoid assuming that it represents only one request location.

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\$_COOKIE' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Cookies are attacker-controlled input.

Never assume:

Cookie
=
Trusted

even if the application originally created the cookie.

docs.title: $_SERVER
docs.text:
High-value keys include:

HTTP_HOST
HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR
HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST
HTTP_REFERER
HTTP_USER_AGENT
REQUEST_URI
REMOTE_ADDR
REQUEST_METHOD

Search:

rg -n \
'HTTP_HOST|HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR|HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST|HTTP_REFERER|HTTP_USER_AGENT|REQUEST_URI|REMOTE_ADDR' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Raw Request Bodies
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'php://input|file_get_contents\s*\(\s*["'\'']php://input' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

$body = file_get_contents('php://input');

This may contain:

JSON
XML
Serialized data
Custom protocol data

docs.title: JSON Input
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'json_decode\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

$data = json_decode(
    file_get_contents('php://input'),
    true
);

The resulting values remain attacker-controlled.

docs.title: Laravel Input Sources
docs.text:
Common Laravel sources include:

$request->input()
$request->query()
$request->post()
$request->header()
$request->cookie()
$request->file()
$request->all()
$request->only()
$request->except()

Search:

rg -n \
'\$request->(input|query|post|header|cookie|file|all|only|except)\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Symfony Input Sources
docs.text:
Common Symfony request APIs include:

$request->query->get()
$request->request->get()
$request->headers->get()
$request->cookies->get()
$request->files->get()
$request->getContent()

Search:

rg -n \
'\$request->(query|request|headers|cookies|files)->get|\$request->getContent\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Validation is important, but validation alone does not make input safe for every sink.

For example:

Length validation
    !=
SQL injection protection

Regex validation
    !=
Authorisation

HTML sanitisation
    !=
Command injection protection

docs.title: Native PHP Validation
docs.text:
Common functions include:

filter_input()
filter_var()
ctype_digit()
is_numeric()
preg_match()
intval()

Search:

rg -n \
'filter_input\(|filter_var\(|ctype_|is_numeric\(|preg_match\(|intval\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: filter_input
docs.text:
Example:

$id = filter_input(
    INPUT_GET,
    'id',
    FILTER_VALIDATE_INT
);

This can enforce the expected type for an integer identifier.

It does not provide object-level authorisation.

docs.title: Laravel Validation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'->validate\(|Validator::make|FormRequest|rules\(\)' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

$request->validate([
    'email' => 'required|email',
]);

Review whether validation rules match the security requirements of the downstream operation.

docs.title: Symfony Validation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'Assert\\\\|ValidatorInterface|->validate\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Locate:

Login handlers
Authentication middleware
Session creation
Token validation
JWT handling
OAuth
SAML
API keys

Search:

rg -n -i \
'login|authenticate|authentication|auth::|middleware.*auth|session|jwt|bearer|oauth|saml' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Laravel Authentication
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'Auth::|auth\(\)|middleware\(["'\'']auth|->middleware\(["'\'']auth' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Common patterns:

Auth::user();

auth()->user();

$request->user();

docs.title: Symfony Security
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'isGranted\(|denyAccessUnlessGranted|Security\b|UserInterface|AuthorizationCheckerInterface' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Also inspect:

config/packages/security.yaml

docs.title: Authorisation
docs.text:
Authentication answers:

Who are you?

Authorisation answers:

Are you allowed to perform this operation?

Search for:

Roles
Permissions
Policies
Gates
Voters
Ownership
Tenant IDs
Administrative checks

docs.title: Laravel Gates and Policies
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'Gate::|authorize\(|can\(|cannot\(|Policy|middleware.*can:' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

$this->authorize(
    'view',
    $document
);

docs.title: Symfony Authorisation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'isGranted\(|denyAccessUnlessGranted|Voter|supports\(|voteOnAttribute\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: IDOR / BOLA
docs.text:
Object-level authorisation is a major source-review target.

Example:

$id = $_GET['id'];

$document = Document::find($id);

return $document;

Critical question:

Where is permission checked?

docs.title: Laravel IDOR Candidates
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'::find\(|::findOrFail\(|->find\(|where\(["'\'']id|whereKey\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

$order = Order::findOrFail($id);

This confirms that an order exists.

It does not by itself confirm that the authenticated user is authorised to access it.

docs.title: Ownership Scoping
docs.text:
Compare:

Order::findOrFail($id);

with a design such as:

$user->orders()
    ->findOrFail($id);

The second approach may scope the lookup to objects associated with the authenticated user.

The exact secure implementation depends on the application's authorisation model.

docs.title: Tenant Isolation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'tenant|tenant_id|tenantid|organization_id|organisation_id|account_id|company_id' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review every security-sensitive object lookup.

Conceptually:

Object ID
    +
Current Tenant
      |
      v
Database Lookup

docs.title: Mass Assignment
docs.text:
Mass assignment is particularly relevant to PHP frameworks with ORM models.

Laravel examples include:

User::create($request->all());

$user->update($request->all());

Search:

rg -n \
'->all\(\)|::create\(|->create\(|->update\(|->fill\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Laravel fillable / guarded
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\$fillable|\$guarded' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review security-sensitive fields such as:

role
is_admin
admin
verified
email_verified_at
tenant_id
owner_id
status
balance
credit
permissions

Do not conclude mass assignment exists merely because create() or update() is present.

Determine:

Input
Model configuration
DTO / request mapping
Allowed attributes
Business logic

Refer to:

Mass Assignment

docs.title: SQL Injection
docs.text:
PHP applications commonly access databases using:

PDO
MySQLi
Framework query builders
ORMs
Raw SQL

The fundamental question is:

Can attacker-controlled input alter SQL syntax?

docs.title: PDO
docs.text:
High-value functions:

PDO::query()
PDO::exec()
PDO::prepare()
PDOStatement::execute()
PDO::quote()

Search:

rg -n \
'->query\(|->exec\(|->prepare\(|->execute\(|PDO::' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Unsafe PDO Example
docs.text:
$id = $_GET['id'];

$sql =
    "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " .
    $id;

$result = $pdo->query($sql);

Data flow:

$_GET['id']
     |
     v
$id
     |
     v
SQL concatenation
     |
     v
PDO::query()

docs.title: Prepared Statements
docs.text:
Preferred pattern:

$stmt = $pdo->prepare(
    'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id'
);

$stmt->execute([
    'id' => $id
]);

The value is passed separately from the SQL structure.

docs.title: Prepared Statements Are Not Magic
docs.text:
This can still be unsafe:

$column = $_GET['sort'];

$sql =
    "SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY " .
    $column;

$stmt = $pdo->prepare($sql);
$stmt->execute();

Prepared statement parameters represent data values.

They generally cannot represent arbitrary SQL identifiers or syntax such as:

Table names
Column names
SQL keywords
Sort direction

Use explicit server-side mappings.

Example:

$allowed = [
    'name' => 'name',
    'date' => 'created_at'
];

$column =
    $allowed[$_GET['sort']] ?? 'name';

docs.title: MySQLi
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'mysqli_query\(|mysqli_prepare\(|->query\(|->prepare\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Unsafe candidate:

$sql =
    "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" .
    $_GET['name'] .
    "'";

mysqli_query($connection, $sql);

docs.title: MySQLi Prepared Statement
docs.text:
Example:

$stmt = $mysqli->prepare(
    'SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?'
);

$stmt->bind_param(
    's',
    $name
);

$stmt->execute();

docs.title: Historical mysql_* API
docs.text:
Older source code may contain:

mysql_query()
mysql_connect()
mysql_real_escape_string()

Search:

rg -n \
'mysql_query\(|mysql_connect\(|mysql_real_escape_string\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

These belong to the old mysql extension and should be treated as legacy code patterns rather than current PHP database APIs.

docs.title: Laravel Raw SQL
docs.text:
High-value searches:

rg -n \
'DB::raw|whereRaw|orWhereRaw|havingRaw|orderByRaw|selectRaw|groupByRaw|statement\(|unprepared\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

These deserve manual inspection.

docs.title: Query Builder
docs.text:
Normal query-builder usage such as:

DB::table('users')
    ->where('email', $email)
    ->first();

is different from:

DB::table('users')
    ->whereRaw(
        "email = '$email'"
    )
    ->first();

Trace how raw expressions are constructed.

docs.title: SQL Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'PDO|mysqli|->query\(|->exec\(|->prepare\(|DB::raw|whereRaw|orWhereRaw|havingRaw|orderByRaw|selectRaw|unprepared\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Refer to:

docs/web/sql-injection.md

docs.title: NoSQL Injection
docs.text:
PHP applications may interact with:

MongoDB
Redis
Elasticsearch
CouchDB

Search:

rg -n -i \
'mongodb|MongoDB\\\\|redis|elasticsearch|Elastic\\\\' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review dynamic query structures derived from:

JSON
Request arrays
User-controlled operators
Filters
Aggregation pipelines

docs.title: MongoDB
docs.text:
Example review pattern:

$filter = $_POST['filter'];

$collection->find($filter);

Determine whether attacker-controlled arrays can introduce query operators.

Refer to:

docs/web/nosql-injection.md

docs.title: LDAP Injection
docs.text:
PHP provides LDAP APIs such as:

ldap_search()
ldap_list()
ldap_read()
ldap_bind()

Search:

rg -n \
'ldap_(search|list|read|bind|compare)\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: LDAP Filter Construction
docs.text:
Candidate:

$username = $_GET['username'];

$filter =
    "(uid=" .
    $username .
    ")";

ldap_search(
    $ldap,
    $baseDn,
    $filter
);

Trace attacker input into:

LDAP filters
Distinguished names
Search bases

docs.title: LDAP Escaping
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'ldap_escape\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Encoding requirements differ between:

LDAP filter values
LDAP distinguished names

Review the correct context.

Refer to:

LDAP Injection

docs.title: OS Command Injection
docs.text:
PHP exposes several process-execution functions.

High-value functions include:

system()
exec()
shell_exec()
passthru()
popen()
proc_open()
backtick operator

Search:

rg -n \
'\bsystem\s*\(|\bexec\s*\(|shell_exec\s*\(|passthru\s*\(|popen\s*\(|proc_open\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Unsafe Command Example
docs.text:
$host = $_GET['host'];

system(
    'ping -c 1 ' . $host
);

Data flow:

$_GET['host']
     |
     v
$host
     |
     v
Command concatenation
     |
     v
system()

docs.title: shell_exec
docs.text:
Candidate:

$output =
    shell_exec(
        'convert ' .
        $filename .
        ' output.png'
    );

Trace:

filename

back to its source.

docs.title: exec
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\bexec\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Remember that PHP also contains application methods named exec.

Inspect context.

docs.title: Backtick Operator
docs.text:
PHP can execute commands using backticks:

$output = `whoami`;

Finding dynamic backticks with simple regex is less reliable.

Search manually around suspicious command construction and use static-analysis tools where possible.

docs.title: Escaping Functions
docs.text:
Functions include:

escapeshellarg()
escapeshellcmd()

Search:

rg -n \
'escapeshellarg\(|escapeshellcmd\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Their presence does not automatically make arbitrary process execution safe.

Review:

Command construction
Argument boundaries
Shell usage
Executable selection
Option injection
Application-specific argument semantics

docs.title: Command Injection Review
docs.text:
Attacker Input
      |
      v
Command / Argument Construction
      |
      v
Escaping / Validation
      |
      v
Shell?
      |
      v
system / exec / shell_exec / proc_open

Refer to:

OS Command Injection

docs.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
docs.text:
PHP provides multiple network-capable APIs.

High-value functions include:

file_get_contents()
fopen()
readfile()
curl_init()
curl_setopt()
curl_exec()
fsockopen()
stream_socket_client()

Search:

rg -n \
'file_get_contents\(|fopen\(|readfile\(|curl_init\(|curl_setopt\(|curl_exec\(|fsockopen\(|stream_socket_client\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: file_get_contents SSRF Candidate
docs.text:
$url = $_GET['url'];

$content =
    file_get_contents($url);

Data flow:

$_GET['url']
      |
      v
$url
      |
      v
file_get_contents()
      |
      v
Network Request

file_get_contents() may access URLs when the relevant stream wrappers and configuration permit it.

Determine actual runtime configuration.

docs.title: cURL
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'CURLOPT_URL|CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION|curl_setopt|curl_setopt_array|curl_exec' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Candidate:

$ch = curl_init();

curl_setopt(
    $ch,
    CURLOPT_URL,
    $_POST['url']
);

$result = curl_exec($ch);

docs.title: SSRF Review
docs.text:
Review:

Scheme
Hostname
Port
DNS resolution
Redirect handling
Proxy behaviour
Network egress
Internal destinations
Cloud metadata
Alternate IP representations

A URL parser is not an authorisation mechanism.

Refer to:

Server Side Request Forgery

docs.title: Path Traversal
docs.text:
High-value PHP file-system functions include:

file_get_contents()
file_put_contents()
fopen()
readfile()
unlink()
copy()
rename()
mkdir()
rmdir()
scandir()
glob()

Search:

rg -n \
'file_get_contents\(|file_put_contents\(|fopen\(|readfile\(|unlink\(|copy\(|rename\(|scandir\(|glob\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Path Traversal Candidate
docs.text:
$file = $_GET['file'];

$content =
    file_get_contents(
        '/var/www/files/' .
        $file
    );

Trace:

file
 |
 v
Path Construction
 |
 v
File Operation

docs.title: basename
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'basename\(|realpath\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

basename() may be useful for some filename-only designs, but it is not a universal path-security solution.

docs.title: realpath
docs.text:
Conceptually:

User Input
    |
    v
Resolve Against Base
    |
    v
Canonicalise
    |
    v
Verify Containment
    |
    v
File Operation

Be careful because:

realpath()

returns false when the target does not exist, which matters for file-creation workflows.

Refer to:

docs/web/path-traversal.md

docs.title: File Inclusion
docs.text:
PHP file inclusion is an especially important review area.

Functions:

include
include_once
require
require_once

Search:

rg -n \
'\b(include|include_once|require|require_once)\b' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Dynamic Include Candidate
docs.text:
$page = $_GET['page'];

include(
    'pages/' .
    $page .
    '.php'
);

Data flow:

$_GET['page']
     |
     v
$page
     |
     v
Dynamic path
     |
     v
include()

Review:

Path traversal
Local file inclusion
Stream wrappers
Remote inclusion configuration
File execution semantics
Allowlisting

docs.title: PHP Stream Wrappers
docs.text:
PHP supports stream wrappers such as:

file://
php://
data://
http://
https://
ftp://
phar://
zip://

Available wrappers depend on runtime configuration and installed extensions.

Inspect:

stream_get_wrappers();

during authorised local testing if appropriate.

docs.title: Remote File Inclusion
docs.text:
Remote inclusion behaviour depends on configuration such as:

allow_url_fopen
allow_url_include

Do not assume remote inclusion is possible solely because a dynamic include() exists.

docs.title: File Inclusion Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\b(include|include_once|require|require_once)\b|file_get_contents\(|readfile\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Refer to:

docs/web/file-inclusion.md

docs.title: File Upload
docs.text:
Primary PHP source:

$_FILES

Search:

rg -n \
'\$_FILES|move_uploaded_file\(|is_uploaded_file\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Upload Example
docs.text:
$file =
    $_FILES['upload'];

move_uploaded_file(
    $file['tmp_name'],
    '/var/www/uploads/' .
    $file['name']
);

Review:

Original filename
Generated filename
Path handling
Extension
MIME type
File signature
Content
Size
Destination
Web accessibility
Execution possibility
Overwrite behaviour
Downstream processing

docs.title: Upload Metadata
docs.text:
Common fields:

$_FILES['file']['name']
$_FILES['file']['type']
$_FILES['file']['tmp_name']
$_FILES['file']['error']
$_FILES['file']['size']

Treat:

name
type

as attacker-controlled metadata.

Do not trust the client-supplied MIME type.

docs.title: MIME Detection
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'finfo_file\(|finfo_buffer\(|mime_content_type\(|getimagesize\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Content detection is one layer of an upload defence.

It does not replace:

Safe storage
Generated names
Extension policy
Execution prevention
Authorisation
Size limits
Downstream parser security

docs.title: move_uploaded_file
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'move_uploaded_file\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Trace the destination path.

docs.title: Archive Extraction
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'ZipArchive|->extractTo\(|PharData|RarArchive' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review archive extraction for entry-path traversal.

Conceptually:

Archive Entry
      |
      v
Entry Name
      |
      v
Destination Path
      |
      v
Containment Check
      |
      v
Write

Refer to:

File Upload Security

docs.title: Insecure Deserialization
docs.text:
The primary native PHP sink is:

unserialize()

Search:

rg -n \
'\bunserialize\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Dangerous Candidate
docs.text:
$data =
    unserialize(
        $_COOKIE['settings']
    );

Data flow:

Cookie
  |
  v
unserialize()
  |
  v
Object Instantiation

Untrusted data should not be passed to unserialize().

docs.title: PHP Magic Methods
docs.text:
Object injection impact often depends on available classes and magic methods.

Search:

rg -n \
'function\s+__(wakeup|destruct|toString|call|callStatic|get|set|invoke|unserialize|serialize)\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

High-value methods include:

__wakeup()
__unserialize()
__destruct()
__toString()
__call()
__invoke()

docs.title: Gadget Review
docs.text:
Conceptually:

Untrusted Serialized Data
          |
          v
unserialize()
          |
          v
Object Graph
          |
          v
Magic Method
          |
          v
Security-Sensitive Operation

Potential operations include:

File write
File delete
Command execution
Network request
Template rendering
Database operation

docs.title: allowed_classes
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'allowed_classes' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Do not treat:

['allowed_classes' => false]

as justification for accepting attacker-controlled serialized data.

Prefer safer interchange formats such as JSON when the data crosses an untrusted boundary.

Refer to:

Insecure Deserialization

docs.title: PHAR
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'phar://|Phar\b|PharData' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

When reviewing older applications in particular, consider whether PHAR handling interacts with:

File operations
Uploaded files
Legacy dependencies
Deserialization behaviour

Validate against the actual PHP version and application stack rather than assuming historical exploitation behaviour still applies.

docs.title: XML External Entity Injection
docs.text:
PHP XML parsing may involve:

DOMDocument
SimpleXML
XMLReader
libxml

Search:

rg -n \
'DOMDocument|simplexml_load|XMLReader|libxml_' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: DOMDocument
docs.text:
Example:

$doc =
    new DOMDocument();

$doc->loadXML($xml);

Do not automatically classify this as XXE.

Review:

PHP version
libxml version
Parser options
External entity behaviour
DTD processing
Network access
Input controllability

docs.title: SimpleXML
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'simplexml_load_string|simplexml_load_file' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review parser options and runtime behaviour.

docs.title: LIBXML Options
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'LIBXML_|libxml_' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Options may materially alter parser behaviour.

Refer to:

XML External Entity Injection

docs.title: Server-Side Template Injection
docs.text:
PHP applications may use:

Twig
Blade
Smarty
Latte
Mustache
Plates

Search:

rg -n -i \
'twig|blade|smarty|latte|mustache|plates|render\(|template' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Twig
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'Twig\\\\|createTemplate\(|->render\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

The critical distinction is:

User input used as template data

versus:

User input used as template source

docs.title: Dynamic Twig Template
docs.text:
Candidate:

$template =
    $twig->createTemplate(
        $userInput
    );

echo $template->render();

Trace whether the template source is attacker-controlled.

docs.title: Blade
docs.text:
Laravel Blade templates commonly reside in:

resources/views/

Find:

find . -type f -name '*.blade.php'

docs.title: Blade Output
docs.text:
Common syntax:

{{ $value }}
{!! $value !!}

Search unescaped output:

rg -n \
'\{!!' \
--glob '*.blade.php' \
.

Unescaped Blade output deserves review when the value may contain attacker-controlled HTML.

docs.title: Smarty
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'smarty|->fetch\(|->display\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review dynamically constructed template source and configuration.

Refer to:

Server-Side Template Injection

docs.title: Cross-Site Scripting
docs.text:
PHP output sinks include:

echo
print
printf
sprintf when later rendered
templates
JSON embedded into HTML

Search:

rg -n \
'\becho\b|\bprint\b|printf\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Expect many false positives.

docs.title: XSS Candidate
docs.text:
$name = $_GET['name'];

echo $name;

Whether this is exploitable depends on the response context.

docs.title: htmlspecialchars
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'htmlspecialchars\(|htmlentities\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

echo htmlspecialchars(
    $name,
    ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE,
    'UTF-8'
);

Context matters.

HTML-text encoding is not automatically correct for:

JavaScript
CSS
URL
HTML attributes

docs.title: XSS Contexts
docs.text:
Review output according to:

HTML body
HTML attribute
JavaScript
CSS
URL
JSON inside HTML
DOM

Use context-appropriate encoding.

docs.title: Stored XSS
docs.text:
Trace:

HTTP Input
    |
    v
Database
    |
    v
Later Request
    |
    v
Template / echo

Stored values are not automatically trusted merely because they came from the database.

docs.title: Laravel Blade
docs.text:
Review:

{{ ... }}

versus:

{!! ... !!}

Do not automatically classify ordinary Blade output as vulnerable.

Review framework escaping and the exact output context.

Refer to:

Cross-Site Scripting

HTML Injection

docs.title: Open Redirect
docs.text:
PHP redirects commonly use:

header('Location: ...');

Search:

rg -n -i \
'header\s*\(\s*["'\'']Location:|redirect\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Redirect Candidate
docs.text:
$url = $_GET['next'];

header(
    'Location: ' . $url
);

Trace whether users can select arbitrary external destinations.

docs.title: Laravel Redirects
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'redirect\(|Redirect::|->away\(|redirect\(\)->away' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Pay particular attention to functionality intentionally allowing external URLs.

Refer to:

Open Redirect

docs.title: HTTP Header Injection
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\bheader\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Trace attacker-controlled data into:

Location
Content-Disposition
Set-Cookie
Custom headers
Content-Type

Modern PHP versions contain protections against some malformed headers, but application-specific header construction still deserves review.

docs.title: Host Header Attacks
docs.text:
PHP exposes the Host header through:

$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']

Search:

rg -n \
'HTTP_HOST|X_FORWARDED_HOST|SERVER_NAME' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review usage in:

Password reset links
Email verification links
Absolute URLs
Redirects
Tenant selection
Security decisions

docs.title: Password Reset Example
docs.text:
Candidate:

$link =
    'https://' .
    $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] .
    '/reset?token=' .
    $token;

Determine whether the host is validated or derived from trusted configuration.

Refer to:

docs/web/host-header-attacks.md

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
Look for state-changing endpoints:

POST
PUT
PATCH
DELETE

Then determine whether anti-CSRF protection is applied where required.

docs.title: Native PHP CSRF
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'csrf|xsrf|nonce' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Token generation
Token storage
Token comparison
Token binding
Token rotation
Protected operations

docs.title: Laravel CSRF
docs.text:
Laravel commonly handles CSRF through middleware for web routes.

Search:

rg -n \
'VerifyCsrfToken|validateCsrfTokens|except.*csrf|csrf_token|@csrf' \
--glob '*.php' \
--glob '*.blade.php' \
.

Review exclusions.

docs.title: Symfony CSRF
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'CsrfToken|CsrfTokenManager|isCsrfTokenValid|csrf_token' \
--glob '*.php' \
--glob '*.twig' \
.

docs.title: CSRF Review
docs.text:
Do not report a missing token without understanding the authentication model.

A stateless API using manually attached bearer tokens has different CSRF properties from a browser application using session cookies.

Refer to:

Cross-Site Request Forgery

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
PHP applications may set CORS headers directly.

Search:

rg -n -i \
'access-control-allow-origin|access-control-allow-credentials|access-control-allow-methods|access-control-allow-headers' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Candidate:

header(
    'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: ' .
    $_SERVER['HTTP_ORIGIN']
);

Review:

Origin validation
Credentials
Sensitive responses
Methods
Headers
Preflight handling

Do not classify permissive CORS as exploitable without demonstrating meaningful cross-origin access.

Refer to:

Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)

docs.title: Session Management
docs.text:
PHP sessions commonly use:

session_start()
$_SESSION
session_regenerate_id()
session_destroy()

Search:

rg -n \
'session_start\(|\$_SESSION|session_regenerate_id\(|session_destroy\(|session_set_cookie_params\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Session Fixation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'session_regenerate_id\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review session-ID rotation around:

Login
Privilege elevation
MFA completion
Password changes
Account switching

Do not infer a vulnerability solely from the absence of a grep match because frameworks may manage sessions elsewhere.

docs.title: Session Cookie Configuration
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'session\.cookie_secure|session\.cookie_httponly|session\.cookie_samesite|session_set_cookie_params' \
.

Also inspect:

php.ini
Docker configuration
Web server configuration
Framework configuration

docs.title: JWT
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'jwt|firebase/php-jwt|lcobucci/jwt|jsonwebtoken' \
composer.json composer.lock --glob '*.php' 2>/dev/null

Common PHP JWT libraries include:

firebase/php-jwt
lcobucci/jwt

docs.title: JWT Review
docs.text:
Determine:

Signature verification
Allowed algorithms
Signing key
Issuer
Audience
Expiration
Not-before
Key selection
Claims

Search:

rg -n \
'JWT::decode|JWT::encode|Configuration::for|parse\(|validate\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Refer to:

docs/web/jwt.md

docs.title: OAuth / OIDC
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'oauth|openid|oidc|client_id|client_secret|redirect_uri|authorization_code|code_verifier|code_challenge' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

State
Nonce
PKCE
Redirect URI
Token validation
Issuer
Audience
Account linking

Refer to:

OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect Security

docs.title: SAML
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'saml|onelogin|simplesaml|xmlseclibs' \
composer.json composer.lock --glob '*.php' 2>/dev/null

Review:

Signature validation
Response validation
Assertion validation
Issuer
Audience
Destination
Recipient
Replay protection
Certificate trust
Attribute mapping

Refer to:

SAML Security

docs.title: Password Reset
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'forgot.?password|reset.?password|password.?reset|reset.?token' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Token generation
Entropy
Expiration
Single use
Account binding
User enumeration
Reset URL construction
Rate limiting
Session invalidation

docs.title: Token Generation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'random_bytes\(|random_int\(|openssl_random_pseudo_bytes\(|mt_rand\(|rand\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Security-sensitive random values should use a cryptographically secure source.

docs.title: MFA
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'totp|otp|mfa|2fa|two.?factor|authenticator|recovery.?code|backup.?code' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Enrollment
Verification
Recovery
Reset
Remember-device
Rate limiting
Bypass routes

Refer to:

Multi-Factor Authentication Security

docs.title: Password Hashing
docs.text:
PHP provides:

password_hash()
password_verify()
password_needs_rehash()

Search:

rg -n \
'password_hash\(|password_verify\(|password_needs_rehash\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Weak Password Hashing
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'md5\(|sha1\(|hash\(["'\''](?:md5|sha1)' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Do not report these functions merely because they exist.

Determine whether they protect:

Passwords
Tokens
Checksums
Cache keys
Protocol-specific values

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'openssl_encrypt\(|openssl_decrypt\(|openssl_sign\(|openssl_verify\(|sodium_|hash_hmac\(|random_bytes\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Algorithm
Mode
Key source
Nonce / IV
Authentication
Key reuse
Hard-coded keys
Error handling

docs.title: Randomness
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\brand\(|mt_rand\(|uniqid\(|random_bytes\(|random_int\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Prioritise insecure randomness used for:

Password reset
MFA
Session tokens
API keys
Invitation tokens
Verification tokens

docs.title: Secrets Exposure
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret|access[_-]?key|private[_-]?key|token|database_url|dsn' \
.

High-value files:

.env
.env.*
config.php
database.php
wp-config.php
composer.json
Dockerfile
docker-compose.yml
CI/CD configuration
Tests
Backups

docs.title: .env Files
docs.text:
Find:

find . -type f -name '.env*' -print

Inspect whether sensitive environment files were committed.

Do not assume:

.env.example

contains real credentials.

Validate the values.

docs.title: Laravel Configuration
docs.text:
High-value files:

.env
config/app.php
config/auth.php
config/database.php
config/filesystems.php
config/session.php
config/cors.php
config/services.php

docs.title: Laravel APP_DEBUG
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'APP_DEBUG|APP_ENV|APP_KEY' \
.

Production debug exposure may reveal sensitive application details.

Verify deployed configuration before reporting a repository default.

docs.title: Symfony Configuration
docs.text:
Review:

.env
.env.local
config/packages/
config/services.yaml
config/routes.yaml
config/packages/security.yaml

Search:

rg -n -i \
'app_secret|database_url|mailer_dsn|redis_url|messenger_transport_dsn' \
.

docs.title: WordPress Configuration
docs.text:
High-value file:

wp-config.php

Review:

Database credentials
Authentication keys
Salts
Debug configuration
Table prefix
Custom constants
Environment configuration

Search:

rg -n \
'DB_NAME|DB_USER|DB_PASSWORD|DB_HOST|AUTH_KEY|SECURE_AUTH_KEY|LOGGED_IN_KEY|NONCE_KEY|WP_DEBUG' \
--glob 'wp-config.php' \
.

docs.title: Information Disclosure
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'phpinfo\(|var_dump\(|print_r\(|dd\(|dump\(|display_errors|error_reporting\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: phpinfo
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'phpinfo\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

If reachable, phpinfo() can reveal extensive environment information.

Verify reachability before reporting it.

docs.title: var_dump / print_r
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'var_dump\(|print_r\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Determine whether output reaches the HTTP response or only development tooling/tests.

docs.title: Error Display
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'display_errors|error_reporting\(' \
.

Review production configuration.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'error_log\(|Log::|logger\(|->(debug|info|notice|warning|error|critical)\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review logging of:

Passwords
JWTs
Session IDs
Authorization headers
API keys
Secrets
Personal information
Full request bodies

docs.title: Business Logic
docs.text:
Search security-sensitive business terms:

rg -n -i \
'price|amount|balance|quantity|discount|coupon|credit|refund|approved|verified|status|role|permission|tenant|owner' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Financial calculations
State transitions
Approval workflows
Role changes
Ownership transfers
Discounts
Refunds
Inventory
Account credits

Business logic vulnerabilities frequently do not contain a recognisable technical sink.

docs.title: Price Manipulation
docs.text:
Trace:

Client Price
    |
    v
Request
    |
    v
Server
    |
    v
Used directly?

Prefer:

Product ID
    |
    v
Server-side price lookup

rather than trusting a client-supplied price.

docs.title: State Transitions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'status|state|approved|pending|completed|cancelled|refunded|verified' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Map transitions:

PENDING
   |
   v
APPROVED
   |
   v
COMPLETED

Determine whether users can skip required states.

Refer to:

Business Logic Vulnerabilities

docs.title: Race Conditions
docs.text:
Look for operations following:

Read
 |
 v
Check
 |
 v
Modify
 |
 v
Write

Examples:

Coupon redemption
Balance withdrawal
Stock decrement
Password reset
Invitation acceptance
One-time token use

docs.title: Database Transactions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'beginTransaction\(|commit\(|rollBack\(|DB::transaction|DB::beginTransaction|transactional\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Laravel Locks
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'lockForUpdate\(|sharedLock\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Their absence does not prove a race condition.

Trace the entire state transition.

Refer to:

Race Conditions

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'ratelimit|rate.?limit|throttle|throttling|limiter' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Laravel Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'RateLimiter|throttle:' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review protection around:

Login
Password reset
MFA
OTP
Registration
Email verification
Expensive APIs
Exports
Search

docs.title: Client IP
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'REMOTE_ADDR|X_FORWARDED_FOR|->ip\(|getClientIp\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

If rate limiting or authorisation depends on client IP, review trusted-proxy configuration.

Refer to:

docs/web/rate-limiting.md

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
PHP GraphQL implementations may use libraries such as:

webonyx/graphql-php
Lighthouse
API Platform
OverblogGraphQLBundle

Search:

rg -n -i \
'graphql|lighthouse|webonyx|GraphQL\\\\|Mutation|Resolver' \
composer.json composer.lock --glob '*.php' 2>/dev/null

Review:

Resolvers
Mutations
Object-level authorisation
Input validation
Query depth
Complexity
Introspection
Batching

Refer to:

GraphQL API Security

docs.title: WebSockets
docs.text:
PHP applications may use:

Ratchet
Swoole
OpenSwoole
Laravel Reverb
Workerman

Search:

rg -n -i \
'ratchet|swoole|openswoole|reverb|workerman|websocket' \
composer.json composer.lock --glob '*.php' 2>/dev/null

Review:

Connection authentication
Message authorisation
Channel authorisation
Object access
State-changing messages

Refer to:

WebSocket Security

docs.title: API Security
docs.text:
Search API routes:

rg -n \
'Route::.*api|/api/|apiResource|JsonResponse|->json\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Map:

Endpoint
   |
   v
Authentication
   |
   v
Authorisation
   |
   v
Input Validation
   |
   v
Business Logic
   |
   v
Data Access

Refer to:

API Security

docs.title: HTTP Method Testing
docs.text:
Compare security controls across:

GET
POST
PUT
PATCH
DELETE

For example:

GET /users/{id}
    -> authorisation

DELETE /users/{id}
    -> no equivalent authorisation

Search Laravel routes:

rg -n \
'Route::(get|post|put|patch|delete|any|match)' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Administrative Functionality
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'admin|administrator|superuser|management|manage|privileged' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Map:

Route
  |
  v
Authentication
  |
  v
Role Check
  |
  v
Sensitive Operation

docs.title: Role Management
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'role|permission|is_admin|isadmin|admin|assignrole|syncroles|giverole|revoke' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review who can:

Assign roles
Remove roles
Modify permissions
Create administrators
Change tenant membership

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'register|registration|signup|sign.?up|create.?user' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Role assignment
Mass assignment
Email verification
Tenant assignment
Default privileges
Invitation handling
Duplicate accounts

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'webhook|callback|signature|hmac' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Signature verification
Secret management
Timestamp verification
Replay protection
Payload validation
State changes

docs.title: hash_hmac
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'hash_hmac\(|hash_equals\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

For signature verification, also review constant-time comparison where applicable.

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text:
Frameworks may process untrusted data asynchronously.

Laravel:

Jobs
Queues
Listeners
Commands
Scheduled tasks

Search:

rg -n \
'ShouldQueue|dispatch\(|Queue::|Artisan::|Schedule::' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Stored input may reach dangerous sinks later.

docs.title: Second-Order Vulnerabilities
docs.text:
Example:

POST /profile
      |
      v
Store biography
      |
      v
Database
      |
      v
Admin Report
      |
      v
Blade {!! ... !!}
      |
      v
Stored XSS

Do not stop tracing merely because input is stored in a database.

docs.title: PHP Dynamic Code Execution
docs.text: PHP contains several highly sensitive dynamic execution mechanisms.

docs.title: eval
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\beval\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Candidate:

eval(
    $_POST['expression']
);

Attacker-controlled input reaching eval() is a high-value review target.

docs.title: assert
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\bassert\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Be careful with historical PHP behaviour.

Do not automatically apply exploitation assumptions from old PHP versions to modern PHP.

Determine:

PHP version
Input
Expression type
Runtime configuration

docs.title: preg_replace Legacy /e Modifier
docs.text:
Old PHP applications may contain historical code such as:

preg_replace('/.../e', ...)

Search:

rg -n \
'preg_replace\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

The /e modifier is historical and removed from modern PHP.

If found, establish the actual runtime version rather than assuming the code is executable as-is.

docs.title: create_function
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'create_function\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

This is another legacy pattern removed from modern PHP.

Its presence can indicate old application code or an outdated runtime assumption.

docs.title: Reflection
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'ReflectionClass|ReflectionMethod|ReflectionFunction|call_user_func|call_user_func_array|is_callable' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Reflection and dynamic callbacks are not vulnerabilities by themselves.

Review attacker influence over:

Class names
Method names
Function names
Arguments

docs.title: Dynamic Function Calls
docs.text:
PHP supports:

$function();

and:

$object->$method();

Search for these patterns manually or with static-analysis tools.

High-value flow:

Request Parameter
      |
      v
Function / Method Name
      |
      v
Dynamic Invocation

docs.title: call_user_func
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'call_user_func\(|call_user_func_array\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Trace the callback value.

docs.title: Dynamic Object Construction
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'new \$[A-Za-z_]' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review attacker control over class names.

docs.title: Variable Variables
docs.text:
PHP supports:

$$name

Search:

rg -n \
'\$\$[A-Za-z_]' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Variable variables can complicate data-flow analysis and deserve manual inspection when influenced by request data.

docs.title: extract()
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\bextract\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Example:

extract($_POST);

This can make attacker-controlled values difficult to trace and may overwrite existing variables depending on flags.

Review carefully.

docs.title: parse_str()
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'parse_str\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Determine where parsed variables are stored and whether they influence security-sensitive operations.

docs.title: Dynamic Properties / Array Assignment
docs.text:
Look for patterns such as:

foreach ($request->all() as $key => $value) {
    $user->$key = $value;
}

This may create mass-assignment-style behaviour even without framework ORM features.

docs.title: Autoloading
docs.text:
Composer typically manages autoloading.

Inspect:

"autoload": {
    "psr-4": {
        "App\\": "src/"
    }
}

Search:

rg -n \
'spl_autoload_register|__autoload|autoload' \
--glob '*.php' \
composer.json

Review custom autoloaders if class names can be influenced by attacker-controlled input.

docs.title: Dangerous File Writes
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'file_put_contents\(|fwrite\(|fputs\(|copy\(|rename\(|move_uploaded_file\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Trace:

Path
Content
Extension
Destination
Permissions
Web accessibility

docs.title: File Delete Operations
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'unlink\(|rmdir\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review object-level authorisation and path traversal.

docs.title: File Download
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'readfile\(|file_get_contents\(|BinaryFileResponse|download\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review:

Path traversal
Object authorisation
Tenant isolation
Content-Disposition
Content type

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\bmail\s*\(|Mailer|PHPMailer|SwiftMailer|MailerInterface|Mail::' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review attacker-controlled values used in:

Recipients
Reply-To
Subject
Headers
Template content
Password reset URLs

docs.title: Header Trust
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR|HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST|HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO|HTTP_FORWARDED' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review whether proxy headers are accepted from arbitrary clients.

docs.title: Client IP Security Decisions
docs.text:
Candidate:

$ip =
    $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR'];

if ($ip === '10.0.0.5') {
    ...
}

This is unsafe if the header can be supplied directly by untrusted clients and no trusted proxy normalises it.

docs.title: Cache Security
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'cache|redis|memcached|remember\(|Cache::' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review cache keys for:

User
Tenant
Object ID
Role
Authentication state
Language
Request headers

Incorrect cache isolation can disclose data across users or tenants.

docs.title: Dependency Security
docs.text:
Inspect:

composer.json
composer.lock

Composer provides:

composer audit

for checking installed packages against known security advisories.

Run from the project directory where appropriate.

docs.title: Composer Lock
docs.text:
Do not review only:

composer.json

because:

composer.lock

usually identifies the resolved package versions actually selected for the project.

docs.title: Dependency Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'"name"|"version"' \
composer.lock

For large files, use Composer tooling instead of manually reviewing every dependency.

docs.title: Composer Scripts
docs.text:
Inspect:

rg -n \
'"scripts"|"scripts-descriptions"|"scripts-aliases"' \
composer.json

Composer scripts can execute commands during package lifecycle operations.

docs.title: Composer Repositories
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'"repositories"|"type".*"vcs"|"type".*"composer"|"url"' \
composer.json

Review unexpected package repositories.

Refer to:

docs/web/dependency-security.md

docs.title: Third-Party JavaScript
docs.text:
PHP applications frequently contain frontend dependencies.

Find:

find . -type f \( \
-name 'package.json' \
-o -name 'package-lock.json' \
-o -name 'yarn.lock' \
-o -name 'pnpm-lock.yaml' \
\) -print

Refer to:

docs/web/third-party-javascript.md
docs/source-code-review/javascript.md

docs.title: Git History
docs.text:
Sensitive data may have been removed from current source but remain in history.

Useful authorised review commands:

git log --oneline --all

Search history:

git log -S 'password' --all

git log -S 'secret' --all

Inspect a commit:

git show <commit>

Use dedicated secret-scanning tools for larger repositories.

docs.title: Backup Files
docs.text:
Find:

find . -type f \( \
-name '*.bak' \
-o -name '*.old' \
-o -name '*.backup' \
-o -name '*.orig' \
-o -name '*~' \
-o -name '*.swp' \
\) -print

These may expose:

Old credentials
Source code
Configuration
Deprecated endpoints
Historical security controls

docs.title: Static Analysis
docs.text:
Static analysis should complement manual review rather than replace it.

Useful tools include:

Semgrep
CodeQL
Psalm
PHPStan
Composer Audit
TruffleHog
Gitleaks

docs.title: Semgrep
docs.text:
Semgrep can identify PHP security patterns and assist with source-to-sink analysis.

Conceptually:

PHP Repository
      |
      v
Semgrep
      |
      v
Candidate Findings
      |
      v
Manual Validation

Official documentation:

https://semgrep.dev/docs/

docs.title: CodeQL
docs.text:
CodeQL supports analysis of PHP source code.

Use it to assist with:

Data flow
Taint tracking
Call graphs
Security queries
Variant analysis

Official documentation:

https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/codeql-for-php/

docs.title: Psalm
docs.text:
Psalm is a PHP static-analysis tool.

https://psalm.dev/

It is useful primarily for type and code analysis, with additional security-analysis capabilities depending on configuration and plugins.

docs.title: PHPStan
docs.text:
PHPStan:

https://phpstan.org/

Useful for identifying:

Type issues
Invalid assumptions
Dead code
Potential implementation mistakes

It is not a replacement for security-specific manual analysis.

docs.title: Reverse Sink Analysis
docs.text:
For large PHP applications, starting from dangerous sinks can be efficient.

Example:

system()
   ^
   |
ConversionService
   ^
   |
UploadController
   ^
   |
POST /convert

High-value starting sinks:

system
exec
shell_exec
passthru
proc_open

PDO::query
PDO::exec
mysqli_query
DB::raw

file_get_contents
file_put_contents
fopen
readfile
include
require

curl_exec
file_get_contents(URL)

unserialize

eval

header(Location)

move_uploaded_file
ZipArchive::extractTo

docs.title: Forward Source Analysis
docs.text:
Start with:

$_GET
$_POST
$_REQUEST
$_COOKIE
$_FILES
$_SERVER

$request->input()
$request->query()
$request->all()

$request->query->get()
$request->request->get()

Then trace each value forward.

This is particularly useful around:

Uploads
Downloads
Imports
Exports
Admin functions
Search
Password reset
Account management
Payments
Webhooks
Reports

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - SQL Injection
docs.text:
GET /search?name=test
       |
       v
$_GET['name']
       |
       v
$name
       |
       v
SQL concatenation
       |
       v
PDO::query()

Questions:

Is name attacker-controlled?

Is it transformed?

Is it bound as a parameter?

Can it alter SQL syntax?

Is the route reachable?

What authentication is required?

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - Command Injection
docs.text:
POST /diagnostic
       |
       v
$_POST['host']
       |
       v
$host
       |
       v
'ping ' . $host
       |
       v
system()

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - SSRF
docs.text:
POST /import
       |
       v
$_POST['url']
       |
       v
$url
       |
       v
curl_setopt(CURLOPT_URL)
       |
       v
curl_exec()

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - File Inclusion
docs.text:
GET /page?page=help
       |
       v
$_GET['page']
       |
       v
$page
       |
       v
'pages/' . $page . '.php'
       |
       v
include()

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - Path Traversal
docs.text:
GET /download?file=report.pdf
       |
       v
$_GET['file']
       |
       v
'/uploads/' . $file
       |
       v
readfile()

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - IDOR
docs.text:
GET /invoice?id=100
       |
       v
$_GET['id']
       |
       v
Invoice::find($id)
       |
       v
Invoice returned

Critical question:

Where is object-level authorisation?

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - Stored XSS
docs.text:
POST /profile
       |
       v
$_POST['bio']
       |
       v
Database
       |
       v
Profile page
       |
       v
echo $bio

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - Deserialization
docs.text:
Cookie
  |
  v
$_COOKIE['settings']
  |
  v
unserialize()
  |
  v
Object Graph
  |
  v
Magic Methods

docs.title: Source-to-Sink Example - Mass Assignment
docs.text:
POST /profile
       |
       v
$request->all()
       |
       v
User::update()
       |
       v
Security-sensitive model fields

Determine whether the model and framework configuration restrict assignable attributes.

docs.title: Broad PHP Search
docs.text:
A useful first-pass search:

rg -n \
'\$_GET|\$_POST|\$_REQUEST|\$_COOKIE|\$_FILES|\$_SERVER|php://input|PDO|mysqli_|->query\(|->exec\(|DB::raw|whereRaw|\bsystem\s*\(|\bexec\s*\(|shell_exec\s*\(|passthru\s*\(|proc_open\s*\(|file_get_contents\(|file_put_contents\(|fopen\(|readfile\(|\binclude\b|\brequire\b|curl_exec\(|CURLOPT_URL|unserialize\(|eval\(|move_uploaded_file\(|ZipArchive|DOMDocument|simplexml_load|header\s*\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

This generates candidates.

It does not generate confirmed vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Input Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\$_GET|\$_POST|\$_REQUEST|\$_COOKIE|\$_FILES|\$_SERVER|php://input' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Laravel Input Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\$request->(input|query|post|header|cookie|file|all|only|except)\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: SQL Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'PDO|mysqli_|->query\(|->exec\(|->prepare\(|DB::raw|whereRaw|orWhereRaw|havingRaw|orderByRaw|selectRaw|unprepared\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Command Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\bsystem\s*\(|\bexec\s*\(|shell_exec\s*\(|passthru\s*\(|popen\s*\(|proc_open\s*\(|escapeshellarg\(|escapeshellcmd\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: File Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'file_get_contents\(|file_put_contents\(|fopen\(|fwrite\(|readfile\(|unlink\(|copy\(|rename\(|move_uploaded_file\(|ZipArchive' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Include Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\binclude\b|\binclude_once\b|\brequire\b|\brequire_once\b' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: SSRF Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'curl_init\(|curl_setopt\(|CURLOPT_URL|curl_exec\(|file_get_contents\(|fopen\(|fsockopen\(|stream_socket_client\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Deserialization Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'unserialize\(|__wakeup|__unserialize|__destruct|__toString|phar://' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: XML Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'DOMDocument|simplexml_load_string|simplexml_load_file|XMLReader|LIBXML_|libxml_' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Template Search
docs.text:
rg -n -i \
'twig|blade|smarty|latte|mustache|createTemplate|render\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Redirect Search
docs.text:
rg -n -i \
'header\s*\(\s*["'\'']Location:|redirect\(|->away\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Authentication / Authorisation Search
docs.text:
rg -n -i \
'auth::|auth\(\)|authenticate|middleware.*auth|authorize\(|Gate::|Policy|isGranted\(|denyAccessUnlessGranted|Voter|role|permission' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Secret Search
docs.text:
rg -n -i \
'password|passwd|secret|token|api[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret|access[_-]?key|private[_-]?key|database_url|dsn' \
.

docs.title: Exclude Dependencies
docs.text:
For most manual searches, exclude third-party code initially:

rg \
-g '!vendor/**' \
-g '!node_modules/**' \
-g '!storage/**' \
-g '!cache/**' \
'pattern' \
.

Later review dependencies separately.

docs.title: Variant Analysis
docs.text:
After confirming one vulnerability:

Finding
   |
   v
Determine Root Cause
   |
   v
Extract Pattern
   |
   v
Search Repository
   |
   v
Review Similar Paths

Example:

Invoice::find($id)
without ownership check

Search:

rg -n \
'::find\(|::findOrFail\(' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Review similar object lookups.

docs.title: Compare Controllers
docs.text:
Example:

InvoiceController
      |
      +-- ownership check

OrderController
      |
      +-- ownership check

DocumentController
      |
      +-- no ownership check

Inconsistency often identifies security defects.

docs.title: Compare CRUD Operations
docs.text:
For the same object:

GET    /documents/{id}
POST   /documents
PUT    /documents/{id}
DELETE /documents/{id}

Compare:

Authentication
Authorisation
Tenant checks
Validation

across every operation.

docs.title: Compare API Versions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'/v1/|/v2/|api/v1|api/v2' \
--glob '*.php' \
.

Older endpoints may contain weaker security controls.

docs.title: Security Review Matrix
docs.text: Vulnerability High-Value PHP Review Targets SQL Injection PDO, MySQLi, raw ORM/query-builder SQL NoSQL Injection MongoDB filters, dynamic arrays/JSON LDAP Injection ldap_search(), dynamic filters Command Injection system, exec, shell_exec, passthru, proc_open SSTI Twig, Blade, Smarty, dynamic templates XSS echo, print, raw template output SSRF cURL, URL-aware streams, sockets Path Traversal file_get_contents, readfile, fopen, writes File Inclusion include, require File Upload $_FILES, move_uploaded_file, archive extraction XXE DOMDocument, SimpleXML, XMLReader Deserialization unserialize, magic methods, legacy PHAR paths IDOR/BOLA Model/object lookup using request IDs Mass Assignment $request->all(), model create/update/fill Open Redirect header('Location:'), framework redirects CSRF Framework middleware, custom tokens CORS CORS response-header construction Host Header HTTP_HOST, forwarded host handling Session session_start, $_SESSION, cookie settings JWT JWT libraries and claims validation OAuth/OIDC Callback and token-validation logic SAML SAML libraries and assertion validation Race Conditions State transitions and transactions Rate Limiting Framework middleware and custom throttling Secrets .env, configuration, source, Git history Dependency Security Composer Information Disclosure phpinfo, debug output, error display Business Logic Services/controllers/domain workflows

docs.text:
[ ] PHP version identified
[ ] Framework identified
[ ] Composer configuration reviewed
[ ] Application entry points identified
[ ] Routes mapped
[ ] Controllers identified
[ ] Models identified
[ ] Services identified
[ ] Templates identified
[ ] Configuration identified

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
[ ] $_GET reviewed
[ ] $_POST reviewed
[ ] $_REQUEST reviewed
[ ] $_COOKIE reviewed
[ ] $_FILES reviewed
[ ] $_SERVER reviewed
[ ] php://input reviewed
[ ] Framework request APIs reviewed

docs.title: Finding Validation
docs.text:
Use the following model before classifying a PHP source-code match as a vulnerability:

CODE MATCH
    |
    v
REACHABLE?
    |
    +-- No --> Usually discard / contextual note
    |
    v
ATTACKER CONTROLLED?
    |
    +-- No --> Continue contextual review
    |
    v
SOURCE-TO-SINK FLOW?
    |
    +-- No --> Not this vulnerability
    |
    v
SECURITY CONTROL?
    |
    +-- Effective --> Protected
    |
    v
EXPLOITABLE?
    |
    +-- No --> Defence-in-depth / contextual
    |
    v
MEANINGFUL IMPACT?
    |
    +-- No --> Low significance
    |
    v
CONFIRMED FINDING

docs.title: Example Finding - SQL Injection
docs.text:
Title:
SQL Injection in Product Search

Route:
GET /products/search

Source:
$_GET['name']

Data Flow:

$_GET['name']
      |
      v
$name
      |
      v
SQL concatenation
      |
      v
PDO::query()

Security Control:
No parameter binding was identified for the attacker-controlled value.

Impact:
An attacker able to access the endpoint may be able to alter the structure of the database query.

Recommendation:
Use a parameterised query and bind the search value as data rather than concatenating it into SQL syntax.

docs.title: Example Finding - IDOR / BOLA
docs.text:
Title:
Missing Object-Level Authorisation on Invoice Endpoint

Route:
GET /api/invoices/{id}

Source:
Route parameter id

Data Flow:

{id}
 |
 v
InvoiceController
 |
 v
Invoice::findOrFail($id)
 |
 v
Invoice returned

Authentication:
Required.

Authorisation:
No ownership, tenant or equivalent permission check was identified before returning the invoice.

Impact:
An authenticated user may be able to access invoices belonging to another user by modifying the object identifier.

Recommendation:
Scope invoice access to objects the authenticated principal is authorised to access or perform an equivalent object-level permission check.

docs.title: Example Finding - File Inclusion
docs.text:
Title:
User-Controlled File Included by Page Handler

Route:
GET /page?page=<value>

Source:
$_GET['page']

Data Flow:

$_GET['page']
      |
      v
$page
      |
      v
Dynamic file path
      |
      v
include()

Impact:
Depending on the path restrictions, PHP configuration and available files, an attacker may be able to cause the application to include unintended local resources.

Recommendation:
Do not construct include paths from arbitrary request values. Map permitted page identifiers to server-controlled template or file paths.

docs.title: Example Finding - SSRF
docs.text:
Title:
Server-Side Request Forgery Through URL Import

Route:
POST /api/import

Source:
Request parameter url

Data Flow:

url
 |
 v
ImportController
 |
 v
CURLOPT_URL
 |
 v
curl_exec()

Security Control:
No destination allowlist or equivalent outbound-request policy was identified.

Impact:
A user able to access the endpoint may be able to cause the application to make server-side requests to unintended destinations.

Recommendation:
Prefer server-controlled destinations. Where user-supplied URLs are required, enforce a strict destination policy and combine application validation with network-level egress restrictions.

docs.title: Example Finding - Unsafe Deserialization
docs.text:
Title:
Untrusted Cookie Data Passed to unserialize()

Source:
$_COOKIE['preferences']

Data Flow:

Cookie
 |
 v
$_COOKIE['preferences']
 |
 v
unserialize()
 |
 v
PHP object graph

Impact:
Processing attacker-controlled serialized PHP objects may allow unintended object instantiation and trigger application or dependency behaviours through available classes and magic methods.

Recommendation:
Do not use PHP serialization across untrusted boundaries. Use a data-only format such as JSON and explicitly validate the resulting structure.

docs.text:
Incorrect:

echo
 =
XSS

Correct:

Attacker Input
     |
     v
Output
     |
     v
Context?
     |
     v
Encoding?
     |

Browser Interpretation

docs.title: Every PDO Query Is SQL Injection
docs.text:
Incorrect:

PDO
 =
SQL Injection

Determine:

Query construction
Parameter binding
Attacker control
SQL context

docs.title: Every prepare() Is Safe
docs.text:
Incorrect:

prepare()
 =
Safe

Example:

$sql =
    'SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY ' .
    $_GET['sort'];

$stmt = $pdo->prepare($sql);

The dangerous SQL structure was constructed before preparation.

docs.title: Every include Is LFI
docs.text:
Incorrect:

include()
 =
LFI

Determine:

Is the path attacker-controlled?

Can traversal occur?

Is an allowlist used?

Which files are reachable?

What does PHP execute?

docs.title: Every file_get_contents Is SSRF
docs.text:
It may read:

Local files
Trusted internal resources
Static application resources
Remote URLs

Trace the input and runtime configuration.

docs.title: Every unserialize Is Exploitable
docs.text:
The function is security-sensitive, but determine:

Input trust boundary
Integrity protection
Reachability
Available classes
Application behaviour

For untrusted input, however, redesigning away from native PHP serialization is strongly preferred.

docs.title: Every md5 Is a Password Vulnerability
docs.text:
Determine what is being hashed.

Password
    -> security concern

Cache key
    -> different context

Legacy protocol requirement
    -> different context

docs.title: Every Raw SQL Call Is SQL Injection
docs.text:
Raw SQL can be safely constructed.

The question is:

Can untrusted input modify the SQL structure?

docs.title: Every Missing Validation Is a Vulnerability
docs.text:
Input validation is only one security layer.

The correct question is:

What security property does this input require?

Examples:

SQL value
    -> parameterisation

HTML output
    -> context-specific encoding

Object ID
    -> authorisation

URL
    -> destination policy

File path
    -> containment

Command argument
    -> avoid shell + strict argument handling

docs.text:
PHP APPLICATION
                          |
                          v
                    ROUTE / FILE
                          |
                          v
                  USER INPUT SOURCE
                          |
          +---------------+---------------+
          |               |               |
          v               v               v
       $_GET           $_POST          $_FILES
          |               |               |
          +---------------+---------------+
                          |

                          |
          +---------------+---------------+

          |               |               |

                          |
       +------------------+------------------+
       |                  |                  |

      PDO               system            cURL

The fundamental PHP source-review question is:

Can attacker-controlled data reach a security-sensitive PHP operation
without an effective security boundary?

Determine:

Source
+
Data Flow
+
Reachability
+
Validation
+
Authentication
+
Authorisation
+
Sink
+
Exploitability
+
Impact

Only then should a source-code pattern be classified as a confirmed vulnerability.

docs.title: Python Source Code Review
docs.text:
Python is widely used for web applications, APIs, automation services, background workers, data-processing systems, administrative tools and security-sensitive backend services.

From a source-code review perspective, Python is particularly interesting because attacker-controlled data can reach powerful functionality such as:

Operating system commands
Dynamic code execution
File-system operations
Network requests
Database queries
Template engines
Object deserialization
YAML parsing
XML parsing
Archive extraction
Dynamic imports
Cryptographic operations

This note focuses on general Python source-code review.

Framework-specific security behaviour is covered separately:

docs/source-code-review/django.md
docs/source-code-review/flask.md

The objective is to answer:

Where does attacker-controlled data enter the application?

What transformations are applied?

What validation occurs?

What security boundaries are crossed?

Which dangerous operations consume the data?

Can the attacker influence those operations in a meaningful way?

The fundamental review model is:

SOURCE
  |
  v
ATTACKER-CONTROLLED DATA
  |
  v
TRANSFORMATIONS
  |
  +-- decoding
  +-- parsing
  +-- validation
  +-- normalisation
  +-- sanitisation
  +-- business logic
  |
  v
SECURITY CONTROLS
  |
  v
SINK
  |
  v
SECURITY-SENSITIVE OPERATION

Remember:

grep match
    !=
vulnerability

and:

Sink found
    !=
Vulnerability found

A static match identifies code that deserves investigation.

Exploitability requires understanding the complete data flow.

Authorised Security Testing

Perform source-code review and dynamic validation only against applications, repositories and environments for which you have explicit authorisation. Source repositories can contain credentials, tokens, private keys, personal information and internal infrastructure details.

docs.title: Review Strategy
docs.text:
A practical Python review can follow this order:

1. Identify Python version

2. Identify frameworks and libraries

3. Identify application entry points

4. Identify routes / API endpoints

5. Identify attacker-controlled input

6. Identify authentication

7. Identify authorisation

8. Identify validation

9. Search dangerous sinks

10. Trace source-to-sink paths

11. Review business logic

12. Review configuration

13. Search secrets

14. Review dependencies

15. Review background workers

16. Review file-processing functionality

17. Run static analysis

18. Perform variant analysis

19. Validate findings dynamically where authorised

docs.title: Identify the Application
docs.text:
Start by understanding the repository.

find . -maxdepth 3 -type f \( \
-name 'pyproject.toml' \
-o -name 'requirements.txt' \
-o -name 'requirements-*.txt' \
-o -name 'Pipfile' \
-o -name 'Pipfile.lock' \
-o -name 'poetry.lock' \
-o -name 'uv.lock' \
-o -name 'setup.py' \
-o -name 'setup.cfg' \
-o -name 'manage.py' \
-o -name 'wsgi.py' \
-o -name 'asgi.py' \
-o -name '.env' \
-o -name '.env.example' \
-o -name 'Dockerfile' \
\) -print

Common indicators:

File Possible Meaning pyproject.toml Modern Python project configuration requirements.txt pip dependencies Pipfile Pipenv poetry.lock Poetry uv.lock uv-managed dependencies manage.py Often Django wsgi.py WSGI application asgi.py ASGI application .env Environment configuration Dockerfile Runtime environment

docs.title: Identify Python Version
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'requires-python|python_requires|python_version|python-version|FROM python:' \
.

Check:

pyproject.toml
setup.py
setup.cfg
Pipfile
Dockerfile
.github/workflows/
.gitlab-ci.yml

Examples:

requires-python = ">=3.12"

or:

FROM python:3.13-slim

Knowing the runtime version matters when assessing:

Deprecated functionality
Library compatibility
Security behaviour
Parser behaviour
Language features
Unsupported Python releases

docs.title: Identify Frameworks
docs.text:
Search dependency files:

rg -n -i \
'django|flask|fastapi|starlette|tornado|aiohttp|sanic|falcon|pyramid|bottle|quart' \
pyproject.toml requirements*.txt Pipfile setup.py setup.cfg 2>/dev/null

Common frameworks:

Django
Flask
FastAPI
Starlette
aiohttp
Tornado
Sanic
Falcon
Pyramid
Bottle
Quart

Framework identification is important because:

Input sources
Routing
Authentication
Authorisation
CSRF
Sessions
Templates
Validation
File uploads

may be implemented by the framework rather than directly in application code.

docs.title: Application Structure
docs.text:
Common Python project structures include:

project/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── routes.py
│   ├── views.py
│   ├── models.py
│   ├── services.py
│   └── utils.py
├── tests/
├── pyproject.toml
└── requirements.txt

Django may resemble:

project/
├── manage.py
├── project/
│   ├── settings.py
│   ├── urls.py
│   ├── wsgi.py
│   └── asgi.py
└── app/
    ├── views.py
    ├── models.py
    └── urls.py

Flask may resemble:

project/
├── app.py
├── routes.py
├── templates/
├── static/
└── requirements.txt

FastAPI may resemble:

project/
├── main.py
├── routers/
├── schemas/
├── models/
├── services/
└── dependencies/
